summary: Partition G into conjugacy classes. Singleton classes are exactly elements of Z(G). For each noncentral representative x, the class has size [G:C_G(x)], a power of p greater than 1, hence divisible by p. The class equation then gives |G| congruent to |Z(G)| modulo p; since p divides |G|, p divides |Z(G)|. Finally |Z(G)| is at least p, so it contains an element other than the identity.
